facts.fact: 章首承接 ch24：她压下一阵委屈——想到吻我就那么令人反感？——追上 Virginia 与 Gazzie
facts.anchor: Repressing a swell of hurt—was the thought of kissing me so repulsive?—I hurried after Aunt Virginia and Gazzie

facts.fact: 她停在几尺外；两个女人都没理会她，已经吵起来了
facts.anchor: Neither woman acknowledged my presence; they were already at it

facts.fact: 她的判断：插到中间只会把怒火引到自己身上
facts.anchor: Stepping between them would have only redirected their fury toward me

facts.fact: Virginia 撵蚊子时嘶声说：你的仆人——想让人整天追着你跑就雇个 PA，你雇得起
facts.anchor: “Hire a PA if you want someone to run after you all day. You can afford it.”

facts.fact: Gazzie：街上随便找个人我信不过；支持我是你的责任，Virginia——连 Mother 都同意 Ida 这一点
facts.anchor: Supporting me is your responsibility, Virginia. Even Mother agreed with Ida on that.”

facts.fact: Virginia 回嘴并首次当面叫出 Gazzie 的本名：我不是闲逛，Gertrude
facts.anchor: I’m not gallivanting, Gertrude

facts.fact: Virginia 说我是在陪女朋友度过正经时间；做你的家务不是我毕生的事业
facts.anchor: I’m spending quality time with my girlfriend. Doing your chores isn’t my life’s work.”

facts.fact: Virginia 压低声音补刀：你不孤单不是我的错
facts.anchor: It’s not my fault you’re lonely.”

facts.fact: Gazzie 的脸转成风暴、危险；说自己的牺牲是唯一的、她重复一遍唯一的原因，Virginia 才能去找那个小面包师
facts.anchor: “My sacrifices are the only—and I repeat only—reason you’re free to go off with your little baker in the first place.”

facts.fact: Virginia：我自己有的是钱
facts.anchor: “I’ve got plenty money of my own.”

facts.fact: Gazzie：你很清楚我说的不是这个
facts.anchor: “You know damn well that’s not what I’m talking about.”

facts.fact: 叙述者屏住呼吸：是否就要知道她们之间为什么总是这么紧张了
facts.anchor: Was I about to learn why things were always so tense between them?

facts.fact: Virginia 指控：你从来就不想让我扮更重要的角色；分给我的全是无聊事——账目、宣传、拉关系——谁都做得了的那种
facts.anchor: Accounting, publicity, networking—things you didn’t want to deal with

facts.fact: Virginia：所以别装作你做了多大牺牲
facts.anchor: So don’t pretend you made a big sacrifice.”

facts.fact: Gazzie 上前，抬手戳向 Virginia 脸前的空气；说你不明白那是什么滋味、那种压力
facts.anchor: Gazzie stepped forward, raising her hand to poke the air in front of Aunt Virginia’s face. “You don’t know what it was like. The pressure.

facts.fact: Gazzie 的对照：你和 Mother 逛复古店、办烘焙义卖、过草莓节的时候，我整条胳膊埋在鳄鱼肉里
facts.anchor: While you and Mother were off at vintage stores and bake sales and strawberry festivals, I was elbow-deep in gator meat

facts.fact: Gazzie 的反问：你以为我不想要休息？不想要下午的迷你高尔夫和傍晚的海滩散步？
facts.anchor: You don’t think I wanted mini golf in the afternoons and evening strolls on the beach?”

facts.fact: Virginia 摊手：怪谁都别怪你自己，看看那能走多远
facts.anchor: “Blame anybody but yourself. See how far that gets you.”

facts.fact: 一声闷响，Gazzie 手里的酒杯在她掌中碎裂，她把碎片丢进草地
facts.anchor: With a dull crack, Gazzie’s wineglass broke in her hand, and she dropped the shards in the grass

facts.fact: Virginia 上前，Gazzie 把割破的手按在胸口，用另一只手挥手挡开妹妹
facts.anchor: Gazzie held her cut hand to her chest, waving off her sister with the other

facts.fact: Gazzie：你根本不知道撑起这个家有多难——因为你是个十足的骗子
facts.anchor: Because you’re a goddamn grifter.”

facts.fact: Virginia 厉声：也不会太久了
facts.anchor: “Not for much longer,” snapped Aunt Virginia

facts.fact: Gazzie 问这话什么意思
facts.anchor: “What’s that supposed to mean?”

facts.fact: Virginia 脸上掠过几种表情：愤怒、犹豫、恐惧；随后挺直、下巴抬高，像在给自己打气
facts.anchor: Several expressions flitted across Aunt Virginia’s face: anger, indecision, fear

facts.fact: Virginia 摊牌：冬至派对后我搬去和 Henri 住
facts.anchor: “I’m moving in with Henri after the solstice party.”

facts.fact: 细节咔哒归位：Virginia 在 Greer House 的明显缺席、她的愧疚——她一直在搬出去
facts.anchor: The details clicked into place: Aunt Virginia’s noticeable absence from Greer House, her guilt. She’d been moving out

facts.fact: 一阵尖锐的背叛感刺穿她；Gazzie 和她一样对 Virginia 的计划一无所知
facts.anchor: Like me, Gazzie had had no idea about Aunt Virginia’s plans

facts.fact: Virginia 显然没打算现在说这些；她朝叙述者瞥来，意识到她全听见了，悔意滑过脸
facts.anchor: She glanced in my direction, regret slipping across her face as she realized I’d heard

facts.fact: Gazzie 说：好吧，抛弃我吧，抛弃 Greer House，我习惯了
facts.anchor: “Fine,” Gazzie said. “Abandon me. Abandon Greer House. I’m used to it.”

facts.fact: Virginia：别扮受害者；你赶走了每个爱过你的人——或者把他们送进了坟墓
facts.anchor: “You’ve driven off everyone who’s ever loved you. Or left them in a grave.”

facts.fact: 她自问那是什么意思；心里跳到 Uncle Leon：是在说 Gazzie 把他锁进 breeding pond，还是另有其事？
facts.anchor: Was she referring to Gazzie locking him in the breeding pond, or was there more to it?

facts.fact: Leon 的那行字浮上来：我要让她放我走，不成功便成仁
facts.anchor: I’ll make her let me go or die trying.

facts.fact: 快得几乎错过：Gazzie 的手掴在 Virginia 脸颊上，啪的一声
facts.anchor: Gazzie’s hand striking Aunt Virginia’s cheek. The pop of it

facts.fact: Virginia 疼得后退，神情依旧暴怒；叙述者说自己比对巴掌更吃惊的居然是巴掌本身
facts.anchor: I was more surprised at the slap than she was

facts.fact: Gazzie 跺着脚绕到屋侧；她正要跟去，Virginia 的手落在她前臂上把她扳过来
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia’s hand landed on my forearm, pulling me to face her

facts.fact: 即便在暗处她也看得出 Virginia 的皮肤变得多苍白
facts.anchor: Even in the dark, I could see how pale her skin had become

facts.fact: Virginia 恳求着解释：我本打算冬至之后告诉你
facts.anchor: “I was going to tell you after the solstice,” she explained, voice pleading

facts.fact: 叙述者连问：为什么不是你叫我来那天？或者告诉我遗产那天？
facts.anchor: “Why not the day you asked me here? Or the day you told me about the inheritance?”

facts.fact: 她咽了下口水，恍然大悟地问：我是掩护吗？好让你搬家时 Gazzie 察觉不到
facts.anchor: “Was I a distraction? So Gazzie wouldn’t notice you moving out?”

facts.fact: Virginia 畏缩、没有否认，只说：什么都没变，Dart
facts.anchor: She winced, not denying it. “Nothing’s changed, Dart.”

facts.fact: 叙述者喉咙发紧：那为什么不直接告诉我
facts.anchor: “Then why,” I asked, my throat tight, “didn’t you just tell me?”

facts.fact: Virginia 抿紧嘴：我以为你知道只剩自己一个就不会想来了；来了之后，我又以为你不会想留下
facts.anchor: “I didn’t think you’d want to come if you knew you’d be by yourself. Once you were here, I didn’t think you’d want to stay.”

facts.fact: 她盯着这个自己以为认识的女人：对方初见就认出她的孤独与渴求，许诺给她一个家
facts.anchor: She’d met me and identified my loneliness, neediness. Promised me a family

facts.fact: 而对方自始至终知道，一旦可以就会抛下她，把 Gazzie 留给她照顾
facts.anchor: All the while knowing she would abandon me as soon as she could, leave me to take care of Gazzie

facts.fact: 像 Mama 一样，把她的人生拿在自己手里、捏成合自己需要的形状
facts.anchor: Like Mama, she’d taken my life into her hands, molding it to fit her needs

facts.fact: 她对 Mama 的摆布已经习惯；没料到 sweet、caring 的 Aunt Virginia 也这样
facts.anchor: I hadn’t expected it from sweet, caring Aunt Virginia

facts.fact: 她说：你在操纵我，声音裂了
facts.anchor: “You manipulated me,” I said, voice cracking

facts.fact: 一层薄薄的沉默滑进两人之间
facts.anchor: A thin sheet of silence slid between us

facts.fact: 她的解读：Gazzie 那一巴掌是在告诉 Virginia——不许把她自己的人生像玩偶一样搬来搬去；就像她对对我做的那样
facts.anchor: she’d been showing Aunt Virginia that she was not to be moved about her own life like a doll. Like she’d done with me

facts.fact: 她的手臂因一股劲发抖；她想象自己的手扇上那张脸、那一记刺痛与余音——又一个丑陋的念头
facts.anchor: I imagined my hand connecting with her face. The sting of it, the ring of it in the air. Another ugly thought.

facts.fact: Virginia 皱眉、卸下面具：别装得好像你没有得到你想要的
facts.anchor: “Don’t act like you aren’t getting what you wanted,” she snapped

facts.fact: 她被这副陌生面孔、以及与刚才甩给 Gazzie 的几乎同样的话砸懵；让其含义沉淀：她没说错
facts.anchor: at the words so similar to those she’d just thrown in Gazzie’s face, I let their meaning settle. She wasn’t wrong

facts.fact: 她真正想要的一直是某个家里的永久位置，而对方正是把她放上这条路的人
facts.anchor: What I’d really wanted was a permanent place within a family, and she’d set me on that path

facts.fact: 她气对方说得准，没话回；转身时差点在草里滑倒
facts.anchor: I was too angry at her accuracy to respond. Instead, I turned, nearly slipping in the grass

facts.fact: 无视正想叫住她的 Harrison，她冲进房子，丢下一句对 Henri 的道谢就夺门而出
facts.anchor: Ignoring Harrison, who was trying to flag me down, I stormed into the house, muttering a thank-you to Henri before I burst out the front door

facts.fact: 屋外蚊虫扑脸、蝉鸣尖叫；Gazzie 的 SUV 已经走了，她只能步行
facts.anchor: Outside, gnats flew at my face, and cicadas screamed. Gazzie’s SUV was gone, so I set off on foot

facts.fact: 走回 Greer House 花了五十分钟，包括几度停下来喘气和两次回头确认没有醉汉团伙跟上
facts.anchor: The walk to Greer House took fifty minutes, including several stops to catch my breath and two to peer behind me, making sure none of the passing packs of drunk men followed

facts.fact: 她一路拒绝想大局：不 wondering Gazzie 把 Virginia 逼走得多狠
facts.anchor: I didn’t spend the journey considering the big picture. I didn’t wonder how badly Gazzie must have treated Aunt Virginia to drive her away

facts.fact: 也没注意到 Gazzie 出手多容易、或 Virginia 挨打时露出的那份没有感觉
facts.anchor: I didn’t note the ease with which Gazzie had hit Aunt Virginia, or the lack of feeling Aunt Virginia had displayed when she’d been struck

facts.fact: 更不去 wonder 她若违逆 Gazzie，对方的脾气能凶到什么地步
facts.anchor: I didn’t wonder just how ferocious Gazzie’s temper could be if I disobeyed her

facts.fact: 她转而闷气下结论：Gazzie 一时的暴烈，是干了一辈子活而妹妹坐享其成的结果
facts.anchor: concluding that Gazzie’s momentary ferocity was the result of working her whole life while her sister reaped the benefits

facts.fact: 也归因于 Virginia 屡次瞒着全部信息把 Gazzie 骗进各种事
facts.anchor: of other instances where Aunt Virginia coerced Gazzie into things without sharing all the available information

facts.fact: 她想：也许 Gazzie 才认识真的 Virginia——一个彻头彻尾的骗子、假货、scammer
facts.anchor: Maybe Gazzie knew the real Aunt Virginia, the one I’d been unable to see. A liar, a fake, a scammer through and through

facts.fact: 但 Virginia 一走，就只剩她和 Gazzie 了
facts.anchor: But with Aunt Virginia gone, it would just be me and Gazzie

facts.fact: Gazzie，脾气像雷暴一样涨落；Gazzie，才刚刚开始容忍她
facts.anchor: Gazzie, whose temper raged and ebbed like a thunderstorm. Gazzie, who’d only just begun to tolerate me

facts.fact: 还有 Harrison——他闪亮的眼睛落在我唇上；她告诉自己那份张力不过是酒和时间一起太多的产物
facts.anchor: but that tension between us was nothing but the product of too much alcohol and too much time together. That’s what I told myself, anyway

facts.fact: 她再补一层：他走前一脸震惊；他对她没那种意思，也 certainly 不站在她这边
facts.anchor: he wasn’t interested in me that way, and he certainly wasn’t on my side

facts.fact: Greer House 逼近眼前，除了餐厅的窗全黑着；没有怪影掠过
facts.anchor: Greer House loomed before me, all its windows dark except those in the dining room. No strange figures passed before them

facts.fact: 窗里只有 Gazzie 走向餐桌，手上一只杯子、头埋在手机上
facts.anchor: there was only Gazzie walking toward the table, a glass in hand, head bent over her phone

facts.fact: 她身后的墙上挂着 Uncle Leon 那幅 Ida 在房子底下挖掘的画
facts.anchor: On the wall behind her hung Uncle Leon’s painting of Ida digging underneath the house

facts.fact: 她想起被毁的速写本、以及 Gazzie 在他死因上瞒着细节的模糊怀疑
facts.anchor: I thought of his ruined sketchbook, my vague suspicions that Gazzie was hiding details about his death

facts.fact: 她自陈信念刻度：对 Ida 或 Ironheart 的鬼她并未全信，但确信一种可触摸的黑暗缠着这个家族
facts.anchor: while I didn’t fully believe in Ida Greer’s ghost or Ironheart’s, I was certain a tangible darkness plagued our family

facts.fact: 黑暗笼罩 Greer House 里活着的每个人、让农场的经营出岔
facts.anchor: shadowing everyone living in Greer House and sending operations awry at the farm

facts.fact: 她拿不准：是两个分开的存在，还是一个
facts.anchor: I just wasn’t sure whether there were two separate presences or one

facts.fact: 一阵战栗撕过她：在 Greer House 待得越久，黑暗会向她显露越多
facts.anchor: A shudder ripped through me. The longer I stayed in Greer House, the more the darkness would reveal itself to me

facts.fact: 但她回不去家——她没有家可回，只有一间闻起来像死亡的空公寓
facts.anchor: I had no home to go back to—just an empty apartment that smelled of death

facts.fact: 这里至少还有 Gazzie，一个接近在乎她的人
facts.anchor: Here, at least, I had Gazzie, who was close to caring about me

facts.fact: 她只剩一个选择：留在 Amelia Island，赢下她的认可
facts.anchor: I had only one option: stay on Amelia Island and win her approval

facts.fact: 屋里 Gazzie 坐在餐桌旁，面前一杯柠檬水，壶在一臂之外
facts.anchor: Gazzie sat at the dining table, a glass of lemonade in front of her, the pitcher an arm’s length away

facts.fact: 她给自己倒了一杯，拉出 Gazzie 旁边的椅子坐下，说我回来了
facts.anchor: I poured myself a glass and pulled out the chair next to her

facts.fact: Gazzie 啜着柠檬水答：我看得见
facts.anchor: She sipped her lemonade. “I can see that.”

facts.fact: 她没指望 Gazzie 突然变成会表达担心或感激的人
facts.anchor: I didn’t expect her to suddenly transform into an emotional person

facts.fact: 但离开桌前，Gazzie 用缠着绷带的手握住她的肩、轻轻捏了一下
facts.anchor: she grasped my shoulder with her bandaged hand, squeezing it gently

facts.fact: 暖意从那个点辐射开；那一刻她知道留下是对的
facts.anchor: Warmth radiated from the spot, and in that moment, I knew staying was the right choice

facts.fact: 她坐到被碰过的地方凉下来为止；客厅里渐深的阴影、一缕极淡的花香，劝她退回楼上
facts.anchor: I sat there until the place where she touched me cooled, and the growing shadows in the parlor, the faintest floral scent, convinced me to retreat upstairs
